title: Protocol for SUMOylome Analysis Using SUMO-T86K Mutant and Lys-C Digestion
author: Wu, Imai, et al.
materials: This section describes the LC-MS/MS analysis of enriched GG-remnant peptides to identify SUMOylated proteins and their modification sites.65.Analyze the peptide samples by LC-MS/MS.Note: In our study, peptides were analyzed using an EASY-nLC 1200 UHPLC system coupled to an Orbitrap Fusion mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Peptides were separated on a 75-μm inner diameter × 150-mm C18 reversed-phase column (Nikkyo Technos, NTCC-360/75-3-155) using a linear gradient of 4-32% acetonitrile over 100 min, followed by an increase to 80% acetonitrile for 10 min and a hold at 80% acetonitrile for an additional 10 min. The mass spectrometer was operated in data-dependent acquisition mode with a maximum duty cycle of 3 s.

This section outlines the computational processing and database searching of LC-MS/MS data to identify GG-modified peptides and assign SUMOylation sites.66.Process raw LC-MS/MS data using Proteome Discoverer 2.5 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) with the Sequest HT search engine.67.Search the data against the UniProt Drosophila melanogaster proteome database using the following parameters:a.Enzyme: Lys-C with up to two missed cleavages.b.Precursor mass tolerance: 10 ppm.c.Fragment mass tolerance: 0.6 Da.d.Variable modifications: acetylation of protein N terminus, oxidation of methionine, carbamidomethylation or N-ethylmaleimidation of cysteine, and GG modification of lysine.68.Filter identified peptides at a false discovery rate of 1% using the Percolator node.69.Perform label-free quantification based on precursor ion intensities using the Precursor Ions Quantifier node.70.Normalize the data such that the total sum of peptide abundance values is equal across samples.

steps.title: Prepare OSC culture medium
steps.instruction: Thaw 20 mL fly extract in a 37 °C water bath, centrifuge 10 000 × g for 5 min, filter through a 0.22 µm membrane, then supplement 154 mL Shields and Sang M3 insect medium with 10 % FBS (20 mL), 2 mL 60 mg/mL glutathione stock, 2 mL 1 mg/mL insulin stock, 2 mL 10 000 U/mL penicillin/streptomycin stock, and the 20 mL sterilized fly extract to make 200 mL complete OSC medium. Store at 4 °C (up to 1 month).

steps.title: Prepare immunoprecipitation reagents
steps.instruction: Make PBS, Hypotonic buffer, Low‑salt buffer, and HEPES‑RIPA + NEM buffer as described; add NEM immediately before use and dissolve by gentle end‑over‑end mixing for 1 h. For anti‑Flag M2 beads, wash 5 µL Dynabeads Protein G per sample with 50 µL HEPES‑RIPA, mount on magnet, discard supernatant, resuspend in 50 µL HEPES‑RIPA, incubate 1 µg anti‑Flag M2 antibody with beads for 30 min at 4 °C with end‑over‑end rotation (15–20 rpm) using a MACSmix Tube Rotater, then wash beads in 200 µL HEPES‑RIPA + NEM for 5 min at 4 °C with rotation (15–20 rpm).

steps.title: Prepare Lys‑C digestion reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare Lys‑C solution at 0.2 µg/µL in Milli‑Q water. Prepare 100 mM DTT, 550 mM IAA, HBS, and Elution buffer as listed in Materials. Equilibrate anti‑K‑ε‑GG magnetic beads (PTMScan HS Ubiquitin/SUMO Remnant Motif Kit) by washing three times with HBS.

steps.title: Prepare LC‑MS solvents
steps.instruction: Prepare LC‑MS‑grade solvents as described, calibrate the Orbitrap Fusion mass spectrometer, and run a quality‑control sample to verify chromatographic stability and mass accuracy before analyzing experimental samples.

steps.title: Generate doxycycline‑inducible SUMO‑T86K cell line
steps.instruction: Transfect OSCs with piggyBac donor and helper plasmids, select stable clones with puromycin, and expand positive clones.

substeps.instruction: Plate 1 × 10⁶ OSCs in a 35 mm dish; incubate 12–14 h at 26 °C until ~60 % confluent.
Prepare two tubes:
Tube 1: 75 µL Xfect reaction buffer, 1 µg/µL pAcM‑HyPBase (1.5 µL), 1 µg/µL pPB‑TRE‑3×Flag‑Smt3‑T86K (1.5 µL).
Tube 2: 75 µL Xfect reaction buffer, 0.9 µL Xfect polymer.
Vortex each tube 10 s (high speed). Transfer Tube 2 into Tube 1, vortex 10 s, incubate 10 min at 25 °C to form nanoparticle complexes.
Aspirate existing medium, add 2 mL serum‑free M3 medium, then add the nanoparticle solution dropwise while gently rocking.
Incubate 3 h at 26 °C, then replace with 2 mL fresh complete OSC medium.
Incubate 48 h at 26 °C.
Two days post‑transfection, passage 25 % of cells into 10 mL complete medium containing 5 µg/mL puromycin in a 100 mm dish.
Culture 48 h at 26 °C, then re‑plate 25 % of cells into 10 mL medium with 5 µg/mL puromycin (100 mm dish).
Culture another 48 h at 26 °C.
Plate 2 × 10⁶ cells in 10 mL medium with 2 µg/mL puromycin (100 mm dish). If few colonies appear, seed up to 8 × 10⁶ cells in parallel.
Culture 48 h at 26 °C, then replace medium with fresh 2 µg/mL puromycin; adjust puromycin concentration as needed (down to 0.5 µg/mL if excessive death).
Continue culture ≥5 days until colonies are easily visible.
Pick an isolated colony with a pipette tip, transfer to 30 µL 0.05 % (w/v) Trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 2 min at 37 °C.
Transfer cell suspension to a well of a 24‑well plate containing 500 µL OSC medium with 2 µg/mL puromycin; culture 3–4 days, refreshing medium every 2 days.
Induce with 1 µg/mL doxycycline for 24 h, verify 3×Flag‑SUMO‑T86K expression by Western blot; select expressing clones.
Expand positive clones and cryopreserve in CELLBANKER 1; stored at –80 °C (up to 1–2 years).

steps.title: Induce and harvest cells for FLAG IP
steps.instruction: Grow selected inducible OSCs, induce SUMO‑T86K expression, harvest cells, isolate nuclei, and perform anti‑Flag immunoprecipitation under de‑SUMOylation‑inhibiting conditions.

substeps.instruction: Plate 8 × 10⁶ TRE‑3×Flag‑SUMO‑T86K OSCs in a 100 mm dish; culture 12–14 h at 26 °C (no puromycin).
Add doxycycline to 1 µg/mL final concentration; incubate 24 h at 26 °C.
Remove medium, wash cells once with PBS.
Add 2 mL 0.05 % (w/v) Trypsin‑EDTA, incubate 2 min at 37 °C; neutralize with 2 mL complete medium.
Collect cells, count, and harvest 1 × 10⁸ cells in a 1.5 mL tube.
Wash cells sequentially with 500 µL PBS then 500 µL Hypotonic buffer containing 25 mM NEM (all buffers must contain freshly added 25 mM NEM).
Resuspend pellet in 500 µL Low‑salt buffer + 25 mM NEM, incubate on ice 5 min.
Centrifuge 15 000 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; discard supernatant (cytoplasmic fraction) without disturbing nuclear pellet.
Wash nuclear pellet once with 500 µL Low‑salt buffer + 25 mM NEM, centrifuge as above, discard supernatant.
Resuspend nuclei in 500 µL HEPES‑RIPA + NEM, sonicate (Branson Sonifier SFX150, amplitude 30 %, 2 s on/3 s off, total on‑time 2 min).
Centrifuge 15 000 × g, collect supernatant (nuclear lysate) for IP.
Add 200 µL nuclear lysate to anti‑Flag beads, rotate 2 h at 4 °C.
Mount beads on magnet, discard supernatant.
Wash beads three times with 200 µL HEPES‑RIPA + 25 mM NEM, 5 min each at 4 °C with rotation.
Split beads: reserve half for Western blot (elute with 2× Sample dye), keep remaining half for downstream digestion.

steps.title: Digest immunopurified proteins with Lys‑C
steps.instruction: Perform on‑bead Lys‑C digestion, reduce, alkylate, and prepare peptides for GG‑peptide enrichment.

substeps.instruction: Thaw bead‑bound protein samples on ice.
Add 2 µL Lys‑C (0.2 µg/µL) to each sample; incubate 12 h at 37 °C with shaking.
Place beads on magnet, collect supernatant.
Heat supernatant 95 °C for 10 min.
Add 5 µL 100 mM DTT, incubate 30 min at 25 °C.
Add 5 µL 550 mM IAA, incubate 30 min at 25 °C in the dark.
Add 900 µL HBS, mix.
Centrifuge 15 000 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; collect supernatant for anti‑K‑ε‑GG enrichment.

steps.title: Enrich GG‑peptides with anti‑K‑ε‑GG beads
steps.instruction: Capture GG‑remnant peptides, wash, elute, and desalt before LC‑MS.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 µL equilibrated anti‑K‑ε‑GG magnetic bead slurry to the peptide solution; rotate 2 h at 4 °C.
Magnetically separate beads, discard supernatant.
Wash beads three times with 1 mL HBS.
Wash beads twice with 1 mL ice‑cold Milli‑Q water, transferring beads to a new tube during the second wash.
Add 200 µL Elution buffer, incubate 10 min at 25 °C.
Collect eluate on magnet.
Concentrate eluate in a SpeedVac to ~20 µL, then bring volume to 250 µL with 0.1 % TFA.
Centrifuge 15 000 × g, 5 min, 4 °C; collect supernatant.
Desalt peptides using a GL‑Tip SDB.
Dry peptides in SpeedVac, reconstitute in 30 µL 3 % acetonitrile, 0.1 % TFA.

steps.title: Perform LC‑MS/MS analysis
steps.instruction: Separate peptides on a 75‑µm × 150‑mm C18 column using a 4‑32 % acetonitrile gradient over 100 min, then 80 % acetonitrile for 20 min; acquire data on an Orbitrap Fusion in data‑dependent mode with a 3 s maximum duty cycle.

steps.title: Analyze MS data
steps.instruction: Process raw files in Proteome Discoverer 2.5 with Sequest HT, searching against the UniProt Drosophila melanogaster database using Lys‑C (up to 2 missed cleavages), precursor tolerance 10 ppm, fragment tolerance 0.6 Da, variable modifications: protein N‑terminal acetylation, methionine oxidation, carbamidomethylation or N‑ethylmaleimidation of cysteine, and GG on lysine. Filter to 1 % FDR with Percolator, perform label‑free quantification (Precursor Ions Quantifier), and normalize total peptide abundance across samples.
